engineering.title: Engineering Decisions & Practices
engineering.subtitle: The choices behind the results, and what each one cost.

d1.title: One database per organization
d1.why: Hard isolation for 19+ healthcare organizations; per-organization backup, restore, and archiving; a missed filter cannot expose another tenant's data.
d1.tradeoff: More databases to migrate and monitor. Every schema change runs against every org database and is read by other services, so migrations are idempotent, indexed and backward compatible.

d2.title: Elasticsearch as a read model for Insight Dashboard
d2.why: The dashboard runs predefined, filter-heavy aggregations (period, corporation, vendor). PostgreSQL stays the single source of truth; the index can be rebuilt from it.
d2.tradeoff: A sync pipeline to run: indexing is a scheduled batch job per organization, so the index lags by up to one day.
d2.outcome: Report load time **40s → 1s**, database CPU **80% → 30%** per query.

d3.title: One engine for Custom Report Builder: ClickHouse
d3.why: Users choose their own criteria over big data. Adding Elasticsearch here would mean two query modes, two code paths, and two sync jobs to keep correct. One engine keeps one path.
d3.tradeoff: Data arrives through full and incremental loads, not in real time; acceptable for reporting.
d3.outcome: Query time **42s → 3s** (over 90% faster); Superset dashboards rolled out to **19+** organizations by cloning.

d4.title: Exports off the request path, on Kafka
d4.why: Generating 1M+ rows inside an HTTP request timed out.
d4.tradeoff: More moving parts: a topic, workers, and job status to track.
d4.outcome: **1M+ row** exports with streaming writes, back-off up to 30 minutes and automatic retries, split into files and zipped, without timeouts; users are e-mailed if an export fails.

p1.title: Clean, concurrent Go
p1.text: Business logic separated from infrastructure through repository interfaces; goroutines, worker pools, bulk loading, transactions, and query tuning for high-volume processing.

p2.title: Tests where the risk is
p2.text: Automated tests covering multi-facility approval workflows, tiered rebate calculations, and lifecycle state transitions: about 450 Go unit tests with mocked repositories, about 150 RSpec files on the core platform, and 70+ front-end test files.

p3.title: AI-assisted PR quality gate
p3.text: Static analysis, security scan, dependency scan, then AI plus human review with checklists for code and unit tests. Review time from **30 to 5 minutes**.

p4.title: Backward-compatible APIs
p4.text: **90+** REST APIs consumed by React applications, kept compatible across releases.

platform-overview.title: Healthcare supply chain platform: architecture overview
platform-overview.desc: React and ExtJS clients call the platform services (Go with Echo, and a Ruby on Rails core). The services read and write a separate PostgreSQL database per organization, send async work through Kafka to workers, and serve the Insight Dashboard from Elasticsearch. An analytics branch moves data by ETL through S3 into ClickHouse for Superset.

insight-dashboard.title: Insight Dashboard: search and aggregation layer
insight-dashboard.desc: Data is synced from PostgreSQL, the single source of truth, into Elasticsearch, a rebuildable read model. The API runs filtered aggregations on Elasticsearch for the dashboard, where users filter by period, corporation, and vendor, then drill down.

insight-drilldown.title: Insight Dashboard: drill-down from dashboard to purchase line
insight-drilldown.desc: The Vendor Performance Summary report works like a funnel. Users start from 10 KPI cards on the dashboard, click a number to see the vendors behind it, then the items, then the purchase history with one row per PO or invoice line. Global filters for period, corporations and cost centers, and vendors carry to every level.

labels.note: The same filters follow the user to every level, and each level has its own shareable URL.

value-analysis.title: Value Analysis: one common each price
value-analysis.desc: Vendor offers sold in boxes, cases, and packs are normalized by unit and pack size to a common each price. An impact calculator then estimates potential savings for a group of items before the committee reviews it.

clickhouse-superset.title: One analytics engine: ClickHouse for dashboards and custom reports
clickhouse-superset.desc: ETL moves data from PostgreSQL through S3 into ClickHouse with full and incremental loads. ClickHouse serves both the Superset dashboards, cloned per organization, and the Custom Report Builder.

delta-build.title: Daily delta build: rebuild only what changed
delta-build.desc: Each build saves a checkpoint. The next daily run collects the report items changed since that checkpoint, rebuilds only their data, and writes it to the report tables. When there is no checkpoint yet, a full build runs instead.

future-price-review.title: Future price review: catch wrong prices before they go live
future-price-review.desc: Future contract prices are compared with current prices per facility and contract. Reviewers filter and search a two-level grid, then approve, reject or pre-reject in bulk. A background job applies the best-contract and non-linear pricing rules and writes the approved price to the active contract prices.
